name: Wisdom tooth removal

card.summary: Surgical extraction of third molars, a routine procedure that looksmaxxers debate when it comes to crowding and jaw development.
card.note: Evidence that wisdom teeth cause crowding is not established; nerve injury is a recognised risk.

quick.overview:
Wisdom teeth, the third molars, usually erupt between about 17 and 21. When they lack room they can become impacted and are commonly removed to treat or prevent decay, gum infection or pain.

On forums, the topic turns on whether to remove them in people pursuing jaw expansion or worrying about crowding. Clinical guidance does not support crowding as a settled reason for removal.
quick.mechanism: Removal is an oral surgery procedure, often with a flap and bone removal for impacted teeth. Postoperative swelling and pain are the common sequelae studied in trials of drugs and techniques.
quick.risks: Removing lower third molars can damage the inferior alveolar nerve temporarily or permanently, reported in about 1 in 85 patients. Other risks include dry socket, swelling and infection.

lead: Wisdom teeth are the rearmost molars and typically erupt between about 17 and 21 [1]. They are the most commonly impacted teeth, and impaction can lead to decay, gum disease and pericoronitis [1]. Impacted teeth are usually extracted to treat or prevent such problems, and some clinicians have also removed them to prevent orthodontic crowding, which is disputed [1].

Removal of disease-free impacted teeth has long been debated. The UK's NICE guidance (2000) opposes prophylactic removal, the American Public Health Association also opposes it, and a 2020 Cochrane review found evidence insufficient to settle the question [1]. Research has found no agreed view that wisdom teeth cause lower incisor crowding [1].

paras: Extraction treats or prevents decay, pericoronitis and other pathology from impacted teeth. Pathology occurs in about 12% of impacted cases, and cysts in roughly 0.64% to 2.24% [1]. Studies cited suggest 30% to 60% of people with asymptomatic impacted teeth need at least one extracted within 4 to 12 years [1].

In the 1970s unerupted wisdom teeth were thought to push front lower teeth together. Crowding has several causes, including tooth size, skeletal growth, age and sex, and wisdom teeth alone do not appear to cause it [1].

Removing lower third molars can damage the inferior alveolar nerve in about 1 in 85 patients (about 1 in 300 extractions), with higher risk for deeper impactions and roots close to the mandibular canal [1]. A review of 339 third molar removals analysed complications after surgery [2].

Many randomised trials have studied postoperative outcomes. A split-mouth trial of dexamethasone reported reduced sequelae after lower third molar surgery [3], a Cochrane review examined ibuprofen and paracetamol for pain relief [4], and a split-mouth trial compared piezosurgery with traditional technique [5]. A randomised trial compared panoramic radiography with cone-beam CT for predicting outcomes [6]. These studies address recovery, not appearance.

A looksmax.org thread asks whether to cancel removal and try midface expansion (MSE) instead, citing upper wisdom teeth stuck behind the second molars; replies discuss expansion, tooth pulling and keeping the lower wisdom teeth [7]. Dental guidance does not endorse these approaches as substitutes for clinical assessment.

timeline.event: NICE guidance opposes prophylactic removal of disease-free impacted wisdom teeth [1].
Cochrane review finds insufficient evidence on prophylactic removal [1].

lore.intro: Forum discussion links wisdom teeth to jaw space and expansion.

claims.claim: Expansion can make room for wisdom teeth so removal is avoided.
claims.believers: A poster says MSE could make space for upper wisdom teeth and widen the smile [7].
claims.experts: No published studies were found testing expansion as an alternative to wisdom tooth removal; guidance on removal rests on pathology and clinical judgment [1].
